installation.note: userdel is a core admin command available on all Linux systems

overview.summary: userdel removes a user account from /etc/passwd (and related files). By default it does not remove the user's home directory or mail spool; use -r to remove home and mail.
when_to_use: Remove a user account from the system
Delete a user and their home directory (-r)
Clean up after removing a person or service account

syntax.description: USERNAME is required. The user should not be logged in; kill their processes if necessary.

options.description: Remove the user's home directory and mail spool
options.use_case: Full removal including home (use with care)

options.description: Force removal even if user is logged in (removes home etc. if -r)
options.use_case: Force delete (dangerous; use only when necessary)

examples.title: Remove user (keep home)
examples.description: Remove user jane from passwd/shadow; home directory is left
examples.use_case: When you want to keep their files

examples.title: Remove user and home
examples.description: Remove user jane and delete their home directory and mail spool
examples.use_case: Complete removal of the account and data

common_pitfalls.description: userdel may fail or behave oddly if the user has active sessions.
common_pitfalls.solution: Log the user out or kill their processes; use -f only if you understand the implications.

related_commands.description: Remove a group (often after removing users)
